title: Introduce control-plane subnet-tenancy, egress policy lifecycle, and DNS-janitor relay
author: Maya Lindgren
description:
Motivation: Private control planes in multi-tenant customer VPCs frequently require more deterministic subnet allocation and carefully managed egress policies. Current installer behavior leaves control-plane ENIs spread across broad subnet pools which makes lifecycle operations (upgrade, rollback, tear-down) error-prone and forces customers to maintain large, permissive security groups and complex DNS conditional-forwarding rules. This PR introduces three coordinated features to address these problems: 1) immutable subnet-tenancy slices for the control plane so instances can be pinned to stable CIDR ranges per AZ and tenant lifetime; 2) an egress-policy lifecycle model driven by prefix-lists and managed terraform resources so we can roll egress changes with a clear create-or-replace semantics (reduces SG churn); and 3) a lightweight "dns-janitor" daemon and Helm chart that mirrors resolver records into a read-only in-VPC resolver endpoint to replace brittle cross-account Route53 forwarding during upgrades and rollback.

What this PR does (summary):
- Terraform: adds modules/pp-controlplane/subnet_tenancy module that allocates deterministic subnet slices (configurable slice_size and tenancy_tags) and exposes outputs for ENI placement helpers.
- Terraform: new prefix-list based egress_policies module with lifecycle = replace semantics and explicit apply-time change detection to avoid transient allow windows.
- Helm/Installer: introduces helm/redwood-private/dns-janitor chart (small Go binary container) and installer hooks to deploy a read-only resolver that mirrors a subset of control-plane DNS records to customer VPC via resolver endpoints. The Janitor uses read-only Route53 API credentials scoped to list/get and incremental delta sync.
- Installer orchestration: upgrade and rollback hooks updated to (a) quiesce egress policy changes, (b) pin/evict control-plane instances from affected subnet slices, (c) ensure DNS-janitor is deployed before changing control-plane endpoints.
- Tests: a new integration test that simulates rolling updates with induced subnet-roll disruption and verifies no transient egress hole and DNS continuity.

Design notes and tradeoffs: immutable subnet slices simplify lifecycle reasoning at the cost of slightly more complex CIDR planning for the customer. We expose parameters to keep default behavior identical to previous releases unless the tenant opts-in (opt-in flag: controlplane.subnetTenancy.enabled). Egress prefix-lists reduce security-group explosion but require customers to accept prefix-list objects (documented in upgrade notes). DNS-janitor intentionally avoids write access into customer Route53 zones; it only publishes a per-customer read-only resolver endpoint to avoid cross-account write requirements.

Testing done: local terraform plan/apply against a test account, helm lint + chart smoke, end-to-end upgrade integration (simulated in CI), manual cross-account validation with partner infra team. See commit log for specifics.

Rollback strategy: installer now performs a three-phase topology switch: prepare (deploy janitor + new prefix-list staging), migrate (pin and migrate instances), finalize (remove staging artifacts). Rollback reverses finalize/migrate while keeping janitor in place to maintain DNS continuity.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Helm chart for dns-janitor with chart tests
- [x] Installer orchestration hooks updated and tested
- [x] Integration test validating egress continuity and DNS behavior
- [x] Docs: upgrade notes and opt-in instructions included in README

Related: ENG-3242 (design doc), INF-88 (customer request), SUP-4123 (support case), see internal doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3242/control-plane-subnet-tenancy

release_notes: Private Installer: Optional controlplane.subnetTenancy feature — deterministically allocate immutable subnet slices for control plane ENIs. Opt-in via installer config.
Installer: Egress policy lifecycle now uses prefix-list resources to reduce security-group churn and provide replace semantics during upgrades.
New component: dns-janitor — a read-only DNS relay deployed into customer VPC to smooth upgrades and rollbacks (Helm chart included).
